Definition: Treating the absence of a mention as evidence that something did not happen or is not true. Silence is only weak evidence, and only when a mention would be expected.
Example: Someone argues, 'The report never mentions safety problems, so there were none.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'The Gospels never record Jesus laughing, so Jesus never laughed.'
HowToRespond: Ask what silence can carry: "Silence isn't evidence unless we'd expect a mention — and even then it's weak."
